proof_summary: Writing the numerator as \(f(N)=N a(N)\), the proof splits \(f(pm)-p f(m)\) into indices divisible by \(p\) and those not divisible by \(p\); product expansions together with Wolstenholme-type harmonic-sum bounds control the aligned part, while generalized Lucas lifting, a finite Taylor expansion of inverse squares, vanishing finite-field power sums, and an inductive weighted-binomial valuation bound control the nonaligned part, giving divisibility by \(p^{4(v_p(m)+1)}\). Cancelling the factor \(pm\) yields the one-step modulus \(p^{3(v_p(m)+1)}\), and taking \(m=np^{r-1}\) gives the required modulus.
